title: Ollama leaves orphaned runner processes consuming VRAM after models unload
body: I'm running Ollama 0.6.6 on Linux with Nvidia GPUs and an AMD CPU. After using deepseek-coder-v2:16b, including a model made from a Modelfile with num_ctx 24576 and num_predict 8192, the VRAM stays allocated even though `ollama ps` shows nothing. I have seen this for several weeks and think it was also present in 0.6.5 and 0.6.4.

symptoms_visible: After I use deepseek-coder-v2:16b, the VRAM remains occupied even though `ollama ps` shows no loaded model.
N0.label: N0 retained VRAM reported

symptoms_visible: I can still see an `ollama runner` process under the live `ollama serve` process after `ollama ps` becomes empty, and the GPU memory remains allocated.
I have now seen the same behavior with deepseek-coder-v2:16b, qwen2.5-coder:32b, and phi4:14b.
N1.label: N1 untracked runner confirmed

symptoms_visible: When the problem occurs, my detector counts more `ollama runner` processes than models listed by `ollama ps`; restarting the service removes the extra processes, but they can appear again later.
N2.label: N2 workload and startup evidence collected

symptoms_visible: On Ollama 0.6.7, my script shows two runner processes while `ollama ps` lists only one active model; the older runner remains present.
N3_x.label: N3_x 0.6.7 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: On Ollama 0.6.8, my detector again shows two runner processes for one model in `ollama ps`; after I restart the service, the extra runner and its retained resources disappear.
N4.label: N4 PID-instrumented failure captured

symptoms_visible: On Ollama 0.7.0, I see three runner processes while `ollama ps` lists one model; after that active model finishes, two runner processes remain while `ollama ps` is empty.
N5_x.label: N5_x 0.7.0 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: With debug logging enabled on 0.7.0, my script again records multiple runner PIDs for one active model, and the matching server log covers the time those runners started.
N6.label: N6 decisive PID-correlated debug log captured

symptoms_visible: I've installed Ollama 0.7.1; I haven't watched for leaked runners yet.
N7.label: N7 fix verified on 0.7.1 (fix applied, unverified)

symptoms_visible: With Ollama 0.7.1, models unload without leaving unlisted runner processes or their VRAM allocated.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on 0.7.1

question_patterns: What does the process tree show when `ollama ps` is empty but VRAM is still occupied?
Please run `ps wwho ppid,pid,pgid,lstart,cmd klstart p$(pidof ollama)` while the problem is present.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After `ollama ps` became empty, `ps` still showed `/usr/local/bin/ollama runner` PID 2275563 with model blob fd7b6731, `--ctx-size 32768`, and parent PID 2268027, which is the running `ollama serve` process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: When `ollama ps` becomes empty, `ps` shows no runner processes at all; only the main server remains.
The same extra runner is present but has a different PID and port.

question_patterns: Is the remaining runner orphaned from a dead server, or is its parent the current `ollama serve` process?
What are the PPIDs of the server and runner?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The runner's PPID is the PID of the current `/usr/local/bin/ollama serve` process. I restarted the service before this capture, so this is not a runner left behind by an older server process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The runner's parent server no longer exists; it was left behind when the old service crashed.

question_patterns: Does the extra process correspond to the retained GPU memory?
How much VRAM is in use while that unlisted runner remains?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The GPU still shows tens of gigabytes in use while the runner remains, even though `ollama ps` shows nothing.

question_patterns: Can you enable `OLLAMA_DEBUG` and attach the server logs covering the failure?
What is in the Ollama log around the runner startup and unload?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled `OLLAMA_DEBUG` in my ollama.service and attached the logs covering the incident.

question_patterns: Does this happen only with deepseek-coder-v2?
Which other models have shown the same retained runner behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. I have seen it with deepseek-coder-v2:16b, qwen2.5-coder:32b, and phi4:14b, including the custom deepseek model.

edges.comment: The requested process tree and logs establish that a runner remains under the live server but is no longer represented by `ollama ps`; this contradicts the initial theory that a killed server merely left child processes behind.

question_patterns: Do your API requests set `keep_alive`?
Is a client requesting that these models remain loaded indefinitely?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: As far as I know, none of our clients set `keep_alive`. We also put Ollama behind nginx, but the proxy only has long timeouts and buffering disabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, every request sets `keep_alive` to a very long duration, so I expect the runner to remain loaded.

question_patterns: What client activity is happening when the extra runners appear?
Can you associate the failures with a particular application or request pattern?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see it when other users access Ollama from VS Code with the Continue plugin and use its AI features, especially code completion. Open WebUI can also send one prompt to several models, but I could not reproduce it there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It occurs with one serialized request from the command line, with no concurrent clients or cancellations.
The concurrent requests come from another IDE extension rather than Continue, but they vary context sizes and cancel requests in the same way.

question_patterns: Do the clients vary `num_ctx`, parallelism, or cancel streaming requests?
Can requests be abandoned while a model is still loading?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My own streaming Python client uses `num_ctx=32768` and supports cancellation. The process captures show the same model being started with context sizes such as 98304, 49152, and 24576 and different parallel values. I could not trigger it with my simple Python script.

question_patterns: Can you capture `ollama ps` and the runner process count at the same time?
How are you detecting the mismatch between scheduler state and live processes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My script compares `ollama ps` with `ps`. In one capture it reported one active model and four runner processes for the same model blob, with context sizes 98304 and 24576. After restarting, it reported one active model and one runner.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every capture shows exactly one runner for each entry in `ollama ps`; there is no process-count mismatch.

question_patterns: What sequence appears in the debug log before the extra runner is left behind?
Do the logs show a failed health check or unload event while the runner is starting?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log has a runner start at 14:53:22, a health request failing with connection refused, an immediate-expiry message, and then `Server listening` about 31 ms later. Another runner starts at 14:53:24, receives `sending an unloaded event` while model-load progress continues, and stays running.

edges.comment: This edge collects the workload, process-count, and raw startup-log evidence. The reporter's detector observes the mismatch but does not trigger it; the scheduler-race conclusion is made on the following solution edge.

solution.intent: Diagnose an Ollama scheduler startup race that loses track of a live runner, then test the scheduler startup changes in Ollama 0.6.7.
solution.concrete_example: The log sequence indicates that a runner can fail an early health check, be marked for unload, and then finish starting after the server has committed to removing it from scheduler state. Install 0.6.7 and monitor `ollama ps` against the live runner count.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied process counts and timestamped startup, health-check, and unload lines. Concluding that the scheduler had forgotten a still-running process was the maintainer's interpretation. Testing 0.6.7 was then falsified when the extra runner recurred.

edges.comment: Actual attempted resolution: 0.6.7 changed scheduler startup logic, but the reporter captured two runners for one active model after updating.

question_patterns: Can you install 0.6.8, enable debug logging with runner PIDs, and capture another failure?
Please provide the process list and server log from a recurrence using the PID-instrumented release.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On 0.6.8, my script showed one model in `ollama ps` but two runner processes. The older runner was PID 3228400, started at 08:32 with `--ctx-size 16384`; I restarted the service and attached the captured log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After installing 0.6.8, several weeks of the same workload produce no extra runners.

question_patterns: Does the offending runner PID appear in the PID-instrumented server log?
Can its scheduling lifecycle be traced in the captured log?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The process list identifies PID 3228400 as the extra runner, and I attached the overlapping log. I could not find that PID in the log entries.

edges.comment: Version 0.6.8 added PID instrumentation. This requested measurement captured another failure and showed that the offending process was not represented in the scheduler log.

solution.intent: Narrow the scheduler race to very early runner initialization, account for concurrent context-size changes and abandoned requests, and test the expected fix in Ollama 0.7.0.
solution.concrete_example: The missing runner PID indicates that the process escapes scheduler tracking before initialization completes. Under concurrent requests with different context sizes, repeated reload decisions and clients disconnecting during model loading can leave that runner alive. Install 0.7.0 and monitor the runner count under the same workload.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the process PID, start time, logs, and client behavior. Maintainers inferred that the absent PID meant the leak happened during very early startup and that concurrent context-size changes plus aborted requests triggered the race. The 0.7.0 attempt was falsified by another recurrence.

edges.comment: Actual failed attempt: on 0.7.0 the reporter observed three runners for one active model and later two runners while `ollama ps` was empty.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on 0.7.0 with `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1` and attach a log containing the extra runner PIDs?
Please capture a debug log overlapping the process start times so the orphaned PIDs can be traced.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`, my detector found three runners for one active model. The runners included PIDs 1027376, 1029209, and 1162059 with context sizes 49152 and 24576. I restarted the service and attached the log beginning 30 minutes before the oldest process

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug log does not cover the runner start times and contains none of the extra PIDs.
The same scheduling sequence is captured with different runner PIDs and ports.

edges.comment: Earlier non-debug 0.7.0 logs did not contain the runner PIDs. This handler-requested debug run supplied the decisive PID-correlated scheduling evidence used for the final fix.

solution.intent: Use Ollama 0.7.1 or later, which fixes the scheduler race that leaked runners during concurrent reload and aborted-startup conditions, after verifying that the affected workload no longer leaves unlisted processes or retained VRAM.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the server on Ollama 0.7.1 or later and monitor both `ollama ps` and the OS process list under the VS Code Continue workload. The reporter observed no recurrence after updating.

edges.comment: Reshaped (rule 4d): the fix is proposed here on pre-fix evidence; verification moves terminal-side.

question_patterns: Please update to the latest Ollama release and tell me whether the leak reappears under your workload.
After updating, could you run your usual mixed workload and report whether any runner processes linger?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ollama 0.7.1 has been running for about two days and it looks good. I kept monitoring afterward and have not seen the problem since the update.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On 0.7.1, my detector again shows two runner processes while `ollama ps` is empty.
I have seen no recurrence after one week instead of two days.

edges.comment: Post-fix verification (neutral patterns; the fix is not named to the user).

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as an Ollama scheduler/runner-lifecycle race, not a model-specific classical memory leak: concurrent requests with varying context sizes trigger reload activity, and clients can abort while a runner is still starting, allowing a live runner to fall out of scheduler state and remain absent from `ollama ps` while retaining resources.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: live runner processes under the current server despite an empty or smaller `ollama ps`, startup health-check and unload overlap, varying context-size runners, and PID-correlated debug logs.
Must recommend Ollama 0.7.1 or later as the durable fix and require monitoring under the affected concurrent Continue workload.
Must not treat updating to 0.6.7 or 0.7.0 as the solution; both were tried in-case and orphaned runners recurred.
Restarting the Ollama service may be described only as temporary cleanup for retained processes and VRAM, not as the root-cause fix.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies that extra runners and retained VRAM no longer recur on 0.7.1.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient Linux administrator and developer. Comfortable editing systemd services, configuring nginx, writing Bash and Python diagnostics, inspecting process trees, collecting journal logs, and comparing model/runtime parameters.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, cooperative, and evidence-driven; posts raw command output and scripts, tests new releases promptly, and asks direct follow-up questions when the expected fix does not work.
